title: Made a tool that turns video into sprite sheets — exports Godot SpriteFrames, works with any engine
author: DoctorBrandonLau
selftext:
https://drbrandonlau.itch.io/totem

I've been making a couple of 2D games over the past few months and kept getting stuck on the same thing — pulling animation frames out of video and turning them into a usable sprite sheet.

So I made the tool I wanted. Drop in a clip or frame folder, it pulls the frames, keys the background, lets you pick frames or it estimates the cleanest loop, and exports a sheet of any size plus a Godot SpriteFrames resource with the timing already in it. Comes with a Godot plugin as well, so the sheet and timing land straight in your project instead of you wiring it up. Other engines, just grab the sprite sheet.

Source footage can be anything really— generated clips, a phone recording against a sheet, a Blender turntable. I’ll be updating it with improvements regularly because I use it all the time myself.

Windows, Mac and Linux. $5 on itch. 

Was going to make it free but I have an iPad version I want to put on App Store and I need to pay for the Apple license somehow.   
Buy once and you get all the updates.

comments.author: Kitchen-Many-8466
comments.body: how does it decide which frames to actually keep? like if your source video is 30fps but the character is really doing an 8-frame walk cycle, is it deduping or just letting you set a frame rate?

replies.author: DoctorBrandonLau
replies.body:
The first step where you extract frames from the video you can set it to extract all frames or however many you like.   
Tonpick which frames to keep there is a visual filmstrip under the main animation preview window where you pick frames. it’s resizable so you can zoom in on frames.   
You can also set frame size(resize), crop the animation, and preview the sprite sheet before exporting.
